## Why This Is Asked

Probes ability to define classification, access control models, SBOM-driven supply chain hygiene, and incident response readiness across automotive telemetry data, financial analytics, and payments channels.

- ABAC/RBAC and least privilege across cloud boundaries

- Tokenization and encryption in transit/rest

- IR playbooks and tabletop testing

```python
# example policy check
def classify_and_mask(record):
    if record.get("classification") in ("PII","PHI"):
        rec = record.copy()
        rec["name"] = "***"
        rec["ssn"] = "***-**-****"
        return rec
    return record
```

## Why This Is Asked

questions.explanation:
DNSSEC builds a trust chain from the Root to each zone using DNSKEY, DS, and RRSIG records to validate responses. A validating resolver rejects any unsigned or bogus reply, preventing cache poisoning. Real-world nuance includes mandatory signing of all zones, robust key management, and timely rollover. It does not hide query content; for confidentiality, pair DNSSEC with DoH/DoT. Architecture: root trust anchor → DS delegation → signed zones → validating resolver. mermaid
```mermaid
graph TD
  Root[Root Zone] --> DS[DS Delegation]
  DS --> TLD[TLD Zone]
  TLD --> Zone[Authoritative Zone]
  Zone --> Resolver[DNSSEC-validated Resolver]
```
